chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him say: 'The Adhan is shortened in travel just as the Salat is shortened; one Iqamah suffices.'

key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: Iqamah (second call to prayer, signaling immediate start)
key_terms.يُقْصَرُ: Shortened (referring to the reduction of elements in prayer or call)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the Adhan and Iqamah for travelers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural aspect of *Qasr* (shortening) prayers during travel, linking the brevity of the Adhan directly to the brevity of the prayer itself. It establishes that a single Iqamah suffices for the traveler, reflecting the jurisprudential principle that the concessions of travel extend to the ritual calls as well, thereby reducing the burden on the worshipper. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between the practices of the settled (*muqim*) and the traveler (*musafir*).
